16:1.sourceText: Συνίστημι δὲ ὑμῖν Φοίβην τὴν ἀδελφὴν ἡμῶν, οὖσαν διάκονον τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ἐν Κενχρεαῖς,
16:1.targetText: And I commend you to Phoebe our sister—being a servant of the assembly that [is] in Cenchrea—

groups.note: The actual Greek ὑμῖν is dative, to you: Paul commends Phoebe to the recipients. The displayed LSV I commend you to Phoebe reverses the roles. The same you lexeme is linked without asserting that its English object role agrees with Greek.
Phoebe is the accusative person being commended in the Greek. The English to before her name is left unpaired with an explicit direction note; it must not manufacture a Greek dative Phoebe.

unmappedTarget.reason: The displayed LSV puts to before Phoebe. Greek ὑμῖν is the dative recipient, to you, and Φοίβην is the commended person. This English connector reverses that commendation direction and is not asserted to be a Greek to-Phoebe relation.
Bracketed English copula supplied in the assembly-that-in-Cenchrea phrase.

16:2.sourceText: ἵνα αὐτὴν προσδέξησθε ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀξίως τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ παραστῆτε αὐτῇ ἐν ᾧ ἂν ὑμῶν χρῄζῃ πράγματι· καὶ γὰρ αὐτὴ προστάτις πολλῶν ἐγενήθη καὶ ἐμοῦ αὐτοῦ.
16:2.targetText: that you may receive her in the LORD, worthily of the holy ones, and may assist her in whatever matter she may have need of you, for she also became a leader of many, and of myself.

16:3.sourceText: Ἀσπάσασθε Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν τοὺς συνεργούς μου ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,
16:3.targetText: Greet Priscilla and Aquilas, my fellow-workmen in Christ Jesus—

groups.note: N1904 has Prisca, Πρίσκαν; LSV uses the extended Priscilla form. These are names of the same woman, as the primary Mounce Πρίσκα entry explicitly glosses Prisca, Priscilla (https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/priska). The form difference is retained rather than silently rewriting Greek.
